text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa met the United States ambassadors to Egypt and Israel to discuss the protocol agreement on Hebron.

- One million feddans of cotton will be cultivated this growing season and in a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, cotton growers decided to free private trade in cotton. Minimum price for a qantar of cotton, about 50 kilos, was set at 500 pounds.
- Annual economic conference to be held March 29-30 under the sponsorship of President Hosni Mubarak.

- Sudan parliament speaker Hassan Turabi says that men who tried to assassinate President Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995 entered Sudan and then left the country for Afghanistan, a French weekly magazine reported.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says eight companies worth 1.8 billion pounds will be offered for sale on the bourse before the end of March.
- Museum showing petroleum developments to be set up in Egypt, Oil Minister Hamdi al-Banbi says.
- Russian companies interested in participating in Toshka river projects.
